facts.summary: Pennsylvania's minimum wage is $7.25 per hour, the same as the federal rate.
facts.citation: Pennsylvania Minimum Wage Act, Act 329 of 1968 (43 P.S. § 333.101 et seq.)
facts.sourceAgency: Pennsylvania Department of Labor & Industry, Bureau of Labor Law Compliance
facts.notes: Follows federal $7.25; PA has not enacted a higher state minimum wage. Verify no 2026 increase took effect.

facts.summary: Pennsylvania requires a tipped-employee cash wage of at least $2.83 per hour, higher than the federal $2.13.
facts.citation: Pennsylvania Minimum Wage Act (43 P.S. § 333.103); 34 Pa. Code Ch. 231
facts.sourceAgency: Pennsylvania Department of Labor & Industry, Bureau of Labor Law Compliance
facts.notes: PA differs from/adds to federal: cash wage is $2.83 vs federal $2.13. PA also raised the tip threshold (tipped status applies at $135+/month in tips) under 2022 regulations; verify tip-credit and dual-jobs details.

facts.summary: Pennsylvania requires overtime at 1.5x after 40 hours in a workweek and has no daily overtime requirement, matching federal FLSA.
facts.citation: Pennsylvania Minimum Wage Act (43 P.S. § 333.104(c)); 34 Pa. Code Ch. 231
facts.sourceAgency: Pennsylvania Department of Labor & Industry, Bureau of Labor Law Compliance
facts.notes: No daily OT. PA's separately elevated PMWA exempt salary threshold was repealed in 2021, so PA follows the federal salary level; PMWA duties tests may still differ. Verify current federal salary level referenced.

facts.summary: The PA Human Relations Act adds protected classes beyond the federal set, including ancestry, religious creed, familial status (housing), and use/handling/training of guide or support animals.
facts.citation: Pennsylvania Human Relations Act, Act 222 of 1955 (43 P.S. § 951 et seq.; § 955)
facts.notes: List taken from PHRC official page. Sexual orientation/gender identity are covered by PHRC interpretation of 'sex' and a 2023 regulation; verify current regulatory status.

facts.summary: The PA Human Relations Act covers employers with four or more employees, a lower threshold than Title VII's 15.
facts.citation: Pennsylvania Human Relations Act, Act 222 of 1955, § 4 (43 P.S. § 954(b))
facts.sourceAgency: Pennsylvania Human Relations Commission / PA General Assembly
facts.notes: PHRA 'employer' means a person employing four or more persons within the Commonwealth. Verify exact 'four or more' wording against the full statute text (Section 4 definitions).

facts.summary: Pennsylvania Human Relations Commission regulations bar denying a person with a disability the opportunity to use, enjoy, or benefit from employment where the denial is based on the person's need for reasonable accommodation, unless making the accommodation would impose an undue hardship.
facts.sourceAgency: Pennsylvania Human Relations Commission (16 Pa. Code Ch. 44)
facts.notes: Confirmed directly against the primary regulatory text (fetched from the official Pennsylvania Code and Bulletin site). This duty is set out in PHRC's implementing regulations (16 Pa. Code Ch. 44, 'Discrimination on the Basis of Handicap or Disability') rather than spelled out in the PHRA statute text itself; related sections 44.13 (equipment modification) and 44.14 (job modification) detail specific accommodation types, not independently verified this session. Applies at the PHRA's 4+-employee coverage threshold (see discrimination.coverage, above).

facts.summary: A discrimination complaint must be filed with the PA Human Relations Commission within 180 days of the alleged discrimination.
facts.notes: 180 days confirmed on PHRC file-a-complaint page (shorter than the federal 300-day EEOC deadline for dual-filed charges).

facts.summary: Pennsylvania's Whistleblower Law protects employees who report or are about to report wrongdoing or waste from employer retaliation.
facts.citation: Whistleblower Law, Act 169 of 1986 (43 P.S. § 1421 et seq.)
facts.notes: Historically applied to employees of public bodies and entities receiving public funds; amended over time. Verify current scope of covered employers.

facts.summary: Wage claims under the PA Wage Payment and Collection Law are generally subject to a three-year statute of limitations.
facts.citation: Wage Payment and Collection Law, Act 329 of 1961 (43 P.S. § 260.1 et seq.); 42 Pa. C.S. § 5525
facts.sourceAgency: Pennsylvania Department of Labor & Industry / PA General Assembly
facts.notes: Three-year limitation derives from 42 Pa. C.S. § 5525 (contract actions). Verify the limitations period against current case law/statute.

facts.summary: Under the PA Wage Payment and Collection Law, wages due to a separated employee must be paid by the next regular payday.
facts.citation: Wage Payment and Collection Law, Act 329 of 1961 (43 P.S. § 260.5)
facts.sourceAgency: Pennsylvania Department of Labor & Industry / PA General Assembly
facts.notes: WPCL requires final wages no later than the next regular payday on which they would have been paid. Verify exact timing language and liquidated-damages provisions in the full statute text.
